text:
maria_g: Heads up — we had a canary induce a traffic surge + regional OOM on staging last night. Can we land a concise fallback playbook for rollouts (model variant fallback, region failover, capacity fallback)?

aj: sorry i missed the incident. quick q — do we want fallbacks to be automatic + aggressive, or conservative with manual ops confirmation?

kevin_r: my vote is automatic but tiered. try model-variant fallback first (lighter quantized), then route to other region, then scale capacity. manual only if all fail.

mar ia_g: ^ agreed. want the console UX to show the fallback chain and which step is active. also need clear guard thresholds.

aj: propose simple heuristics:
- error_rate > 1% for 60s => step 1 (variant fallback)
- p95 latency > 2x baseline for 120s => step 1
- if step1 fails within 3m (error_rate still >1%) => step 2 (regional failover)
- if capacity saturation (GPU mem pressure > 85%) => immediate step2

kevin_r: here's a config snippet I prototyped for routing-policy service:```yaml
name: canary_fallback_policy
canary: true
steps:
  - name: variant_fallback
    trigger:
      error_rate_pct: 1
      window_s: 60
    action:
      replace_with: model_variant:quant-8b
      traffic_shift: 100\n  - name: regional_failover
    trigger:
      error_rate_pct: 1
      window_s: 180
    action:
      route: other_region
      traffic_shift: 100
  - name: capacity_burst
    trigger:
      gpu_mem_pct: 85
    action:
      enqueue_with_burst_pool: true
      route: other_region```

tamara: love the yaml. a few concerns: 1) rolling back to quantized model can change outputs — need an integrity check + shadowing to compare. 2) region failover should respect data residency tags (EU vs US).

maria_g: yes on both. add an automatic validation step that runs a small eval set on the fallback variant before full switch (timebox 15s). and policy should be allowed to mark "data-residency-locked" so regional failover is skipped.

aj: how does this surface in console and alerts? we need 3 things: real-time banner, per-route timeline with active step, and a synthesized incident (auto-created) if we escalate to region failover.

infra-bot: deploy-check: policy updated in staging at 1765123520 by kevin_r.

kevin_r: re: console, i'll add a small widget: "Fallback timeline" + toggle to expand the config. Also add per-step metrics (invocations, errors, latency, model delta score).

tamara: on the telemetry side — add a derived metric: fallback_delta_quality = (baseline_quality - fallback_quality) aggregated by prompt-set. feed into Optimize alerts so ML team gets notified if quality regresses > 2% after fallback.

maria_g: can we also add a pre-rollout checklist: shadow run for 5 minutes at 5% traffic with quality diff < 1% before canary promotion? ops can skip for emergency hotfixes.

aj: +1. Also we need an emergency circuit-breaker: if global error_rate > 5% for 30s, route all traffic to last known-good model and page SRE.

kevin_r: i'll sketch UI + API changes: 1) routing-policy API adds "fallback_chain" with ordered steps 2) rollout api gets new flags: enforce_data_residency, shadow_check_timeout_s 3) console shows granular step-level toggles.

maria_g: thanks. action items: @kevin_r to open PR with config schema + console mock; @tamara to add telemetry metrics and Optimize hook; @aj to write short playbook doc for oncall. I'll run the staging test tomorrow and post results.

sre-bot: page created: #oncall-incidents if circuit-breaker trips.

kevin_r: PR opened: https://git.internal/r/redwood/platform/pulls/624 (WIP). I'll add the mock images there.

maria_g: perfect. small followup: can we include a simulated load test in the PR pipeline to validate memory-triggered capacity fallback?

kevin_r: yes, adding k6 script + synthetic GPU mem pressure via test container. will run on PR.

tamara: great. if we can get this merged this week we can roll to staging and iterate on UX. :thumbsup:
